# Welcome to *How LLMs work (demo)*

This is a short demo topic. The plan: how text becomes numbers, how the model picks the next token, how attention mixes tokens, and how it's all trained. Everything lives on the [cheat sheet](wiki:home) and in the [glossary](wiki:glossary).

```viz flow
{ nodes: [
    {id: "t", label: "text"},
    {id: "tok", label: "tokens", sub: "IDs", key: "tok"},
    {id: "emb", label: "embedding rows", key: "x"},
    {id: "blk", label: "N × block", sub: "attention + MLP", key: "blk"},
    {id: "lg", label: "logits", sub: "one per vocab entry", key: "logits"},
    {id: "p", label: "softmax", key: "p"} ],
  edges: [["t", "tok", "split"], ["tok", "emb", "lookup"]] }
```

{{Tokens|tok}} pick {{embedding rows|x}}, the {{blocks|blk}} refine them, and the last position becomes {{logits|logits}} and then {{probabilities|p}}.

:::note
Levels go from 0 (never seen it) to 5 (could teach it). Dashed boxes on the [concept map](map:tok) are fog: things we haven't covered yet.
:::

:::question
Before we start: what do you think the model actually receives as input when you type a sentence? One or two sentences is plenty.
:::
I think the text gets chopped into pieces, roughly words or parts of words, and each piece becomes a number the model looks up somewhere.

note: knew text is split into sub-word tokens mapped to IDs

text:
Right, that's the core of it ([your answer](msg:2026-01-05.3)). Some detail:

A [tokenizer](term:tokenizer) splits text into chunks from a fixed [vocabulary](term:vocabulary), and each chunk has an integer ID:

```viz tokens
{ tokens: ["The", " river", " bank", " was", " muddy"], keys: ["the", "river", "bank", "was", "muddy"],
  caption: "Five tokens. The leading spaces are part of the token." }
```

| text | tokens | why |
|---|---|---|
| `bank` | `bank` | common word: one token |
| `unbankable` | `un` `bank` `able` | rare word: pieces |
| `2026` | `202` `6` | numbers split by frequency |

Each ID is just a row number into the embedding table: the model looks up that row and starts from those numbers.

:::insight
The ID itself carries no meaning. Token 4821 and token 4822 are no more related than 4821 and 17.
:::

:::question
Why would it be a bad idea to feed the raw ID number (say 4821) straight into the network as its input?
:::

Sure. The network treats its inputs as **quantities**. If "bank" were 4821 and "ukulele" 4822, every computation would see them as almost the same input, and a single number can only say "more" or "less" of one thing. A learned row of many numbers per token avoids both problems ([tokens recap](msg:2026-01-05.5)).

## From the last vector to logits

At the top of the model, the last position's vector {{x|x}} is compared against one column per vocabulary token in {{W_U|wu}}. The result is one score per token: the {{logits|z}}.

$$\k{z}{z} = \k{x}{x}\,\k{wu}{W_U}$$

```viz vector
{ name: "x", values: [0.9, -0.4, 0.3], labels: ["d1", "d2", "d3"], key: "x", heat: true }
```

```viz matrix
{ name: "W_U", key: "wu", rows: [[1.2, -0.5, 0.1, 0.0], [0.3, 0.8, -1.0, 0.2], [0.5, 0.1, 0.4, -0.6]],
  rowLabels: ["d1", "d2", "d3"], colLabels: ["river", "money", "the", "fish"],
  colKeys: ["river z", "money z", "the z", "fish z"], heat: true, digits: 1,
  caption: "One column per vocabulary token. Real models: 4096 rows × 32k columns." }
```

:::question
The logit for "river" is the dot product of x with the river column. In your own words, what does a high logit mean about how x and that column relate?
:::
A high logit means x and the river column have big numbers in the same places, so the model thinks river is likely. So the logit is basically already the probability?

note: alignment right; thinks logits are already probabilities

text:
The first half is right: a high logit means $x$ points the same way as that column. The second half isn't: logits are **not probabilities**. They can be negative and don't sum to anything in particular. [Softmax](term:softmax) turns them into probabilities:

$$p_i = \frac{e^{z_i / T}}{\sum_j e^{z_j / T}}$$

where $T$ is the [temperature](term:temperature). Play with it:

```viz softmax
{ logits: [{label: "river", value: 2.0, key: "river"}, {label: "money", value: 1.0, key: "money"},
           {label: "the", value: -0.5, key: "the"}, {label: "fish", value: 0.2, key: "fish"}],
  temperature: 1 }
```

:::warn
A logit of 0 does **not** mean probability 0. Only the differences between logits matter: adding 5 to all of them changes nothing.
:::

:::question
What happens to the probabilities as T gets very small (close to 0)? And as T gets large?
:::

> Only the differences between logits matter: adding 5 to all of them changes nothing.

Why is that? Adding 5 makes every number bigger, so shouldn't something change?

Because $e^{z+5} = e^5 \cdot e^z$. Every term on the top **and** the bottom of the fraction gets the same factor $e^5$, and it cancels. That's also why implementations subtract the max first, for numerical safety:

```python
import math

def softmax(z, T=1.0):
    m = max(z)
    ex = [math.exp((v - m) / T) for v in z]
    s = sum(ex)
    return [e / s for e in ex]
```

For two tokens, the probability of the first depends only on the gap $d = z_1 - z_2$:

```viz plot
{ x: [-6, 6], y: [0, 1],
  fns: [{ f: "1/(1+exp(-x/T))", label: "p(first) vs gap d", key: "p1" }],
  sliders: [{ name: "T", label: "temperature T", min: 0.1, max: 4, value: 1, step: 0.05 }],
  caption: "Shift both logits by the same amount and d doesn't change, so neither does p." }
```

:::tip
When you see "logits" in code, think "unnormalised log-probabilities": softmax is the only step between them and probabilities.
:::
Small T stretches the gaps, so the top token takes almost everything, like always picking the max. Large T squashes the gaps and everything gets closer to equal.

note: both limits right, with the reason (gaps scaled by 1/T)

text:
Exactly. [Temperature](skill:3.2) only rescales the gaps.

:::recap
- Text → tokens → IDs; the ID is only a row number ([tokens](msg:2026-01-05.5), [why not raw IDs](msg:2026-01-05.7)).
- The last vector times W_U gives one logit per token ([logits](msg:2026-01-05.7)).
- Softmax turns logits into probabilities; T scales the gaps ([softmax](msg:2026-01-05.10), [shift invariance](msg:2026-01-05.12)).
:::

Next time: [attention](skill:4.1), how tokens look at each other.
